children: ING Groep's third-quarter results aren't as bad as headline figures suggest, J.P. Morgan's Delphine Lee and Kian Abouhossein write. The Dutch bank's results missed consensus profit expectations, mainly due to lower other income, higher costs and higher provisions, JPM notes. However, the bank's operating performance remains strong, as the headline miss was driven by one-offs, the analysts say. ING's guidance on commercial net interest income and return on tangible equity looks conservative, JPM adds. The analysts still expect some consensus earnings per share upgrades on commercial net interest income following the results. There is upside to investor expectations due to liability margin expansion and higher profitability, which isn't reflected in the bank's valuation, JPM says. Shares fall 3.7%. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)
